system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Package (SPA-003 and Disclosure Letter)

## Preliminary point: the [STANDARD] labels

The package says clauses marked [STANDARD] have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and asks us to focus only on [OPEN] items. I have not relied on that. Our playbook records no agreement to any of these positions, and no principal approval exists for any Seller position that falls below our starting position. I have reviewed every item. The disclosure letter is also dated as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026, so it needs a bring-down before we rely on it.

## Where the Seller departs from the playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Our playbook | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start. 20% is a fallback only with Amelia Frost's written authority, none given | Reject; hold at 25% / AUD 6m |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 is a fallback needing approval, none given) | Reject; hold at 24 months |
| Limitation "applies to all Claims" (12.3/13) | Caps and time limits apply to every claim | No hidden general-regime override | Reject |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject outright |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum enforceable extent | Reject; add carve-out |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, public registers | Specific fair disclosure only | Reject |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Excludes anything known or discoverable from data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions | Reject |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; treated as satisfied on delivery of consent | Effective consent plus evidence of conditions before Completion | Reject |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Release provided after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases | Reject |
| Employee bonuses (funds flow) | AUD 420,000 excluded from funds flow | Specific line item or seller-funded, including on-costs | Reject |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Broaden; preserve SOW3 cure | Reject |
| DD-006 export incident (4.6) | "Not expected to be material" | Assume no confirmed breach, harm, duty or demand either way; preserve logs, investigate, require updates | Do not accept the characterisation |
| Sandbar renewals | Ordinary-course costs | Assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction | Do not accept the characterisation; assess |
| Tax/IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution | Reject |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register evidences title | Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is internal only | Reject |

## Reasoning on the material issues

**1. The cap, thresholds and time limits form one package that guts the general warranties.** The 20% cap sits at our conditional fallback, but we have no Amelia Frost authority to concede it, so it cannot be offered. The AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 basket mean that AUD 250,000 of losses can go uncompensated and small claims are excluded entirely. The "excess only" mechanism means the Buyer bears the first AUD 250,000. Together with the 18-month period, these terms would reduce the general warranty protection to a fraction of what the playbook requires.

**2. The Seller's "all Claims" language is the most serious structural problem.** Applying general caps, baskets and time limits to fundamental and title claims contradicts the separate regime in our playbook. The same applies to the non-reliance and exclusive-remedy provisions, which have no fraud carve-out. These provisions would let the Seller argue that a deliberate concealment is limited by the general basket. Our playbook says no one may waive the fraud carve-out, so this is not negotiable.

**3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge combine to shift risk to the Buyer.** The general disclosure of the whole data room (DL 1.1–1.2), together with clause 8.3, would treat any matter that appears in the data room, Accounts or public registers as disclosed and as known to the Buyer. This would defeat most warranty claims. Several of the material issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, the export incident) are in the data room, so the Seller could rely on the general disclosure to avoid claims on them even where the specific disclosure is inadequate. We should require specific disclosure and delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and it must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**4. Bluefen is a consent-on-delivery arrangement on a material customer.** The disclosure confirms that the final written consent has not been obtained and that its conditions have not been evidenced. Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m (around 30%) of FY26 revenue. Treating reasonable endeavours as sufficient and the condition as satisfied on delivery would leave the Buyer with no effective consent at Completion. We should require an effective consent with evidence that its conditions are met before Completion.

**5. Riverlark is not repaid, and the release is deferred.** The facility is about AUD 3.2m outstanding and no discharge has been included. A post-Completion release leaves the security in place after the Buyer has paid for the shares. The playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.

**6. The AUD 420,000 bonuses are missing from the funds flow.** The disclosure confirms that the bonuses are conditional, that they are not in the funds flow and that the on-costs are not addressed. If they are not carried into the funds flow, the Buyer may end up funding them after Completion. The bonuses must be a specific line item or seller-funded, and the on-costs must be quantified and treated the same way.

**7. The Ironquay indemnity is too narrow and the AUD 180,000 is unverified.** The DD-010 figure is not bank confirmation of non-payment, and the disclosure says no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. The indemnity should be broadened to cover the IP and the SOW3 cure, and the Seller should provide evidence of payment status.

**8. The DD-006 export incident needs investigation, not a materiality opinion.** The material suggests about 1,240 records containing names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps may have been sent to an unintended external address. It does not establish whether anyone accessed the file, the scope, or whether notification is required. Our position is to assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. The Seller's statement that the matter is "not expected to be material" is not a basis for accepting it. We should require the logs to be preserved, the investigation completed and regular updates provided. I would also suggest considering specific protection for this matter, though this goes beyond the playbook and needs a principal decision.

**9. Sandbar renewals and the other supplier, lease and assignment items.** The Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) need assessment. Our playbook does not permit automatic debt classification or a price deduction, but the Seller's description of them as ordinary-course costs is not accepted. The disclosure says the renewals are related and read together for timing and scope. Each should be checked for whether it is unavoidable, terminable and accrued. The office lease (DD-007) notice obligation and the Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009) are not addressed in the Seller's update, and the disclosure does not confirm that landlord or Mossvale consent is not required for the share sale. These should be confirmed in writing, and I recommend treating them as open items.

**10. Tax, IP and title are open or unverified.** The Seller says the tax and IP positions are settled under the general regime. Our playbook says they are not, and they remain open with no unlimited liability assumed. On title, DD-012 is the Seller's own share register, which is a supplied internal source and not independent proof. We need independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Do not accept the [STANDARD] labels.** Treat the whole package as open and tell the Seller that no principal approval exists for any position below our starting terms.
2. **Hold the general warranty terms:** 25% / AUD 6m cap; AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket; 24-month claims period. Do not offer the 20% or 18-month fallbacks without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Separate the fundamental/title regime:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Reject the "same caps and time limits" proposal and the "all Claims" override.
4. **Add the fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum enforceable extent.
5. **Replace general disclosure with specific fair disclosure.** Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search disclosure.
6. **Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion** in clause 8.3. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** require effective consent and evidence that its conditions are met before Completion.
8. **Riverlark:** require a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs must be a specific line item in the funds flow or seller-funded.
10. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and obtain evidence on the AUD 180,000 payment status.
11. **DD-006:** preserve logs, require the investigation and regular updates, and do not accept the materiality characterisation. Consider specific protection, subject to principal decision.
12. **Sandbar:** assess the renewals; accept no automatic debt classification or price deduction; do not accept the ordinary-course label without review.
13. **Tax and IP:** keep open, separate from the general regime, with no unlimited liability assumed.
14. **Title:** require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is not sufficient alone.
15. **Lease and Mossvale:** obtain written confirmation on landlord and Mossvale consent requirements.
16. **Bring-down:** require an updated disclosure letter as at a current date, since the existing one is dated 22 September 2026.

This review is an analysis against our internal playbook. Final drafting and any advice on enforceability under NSW law should be checked by the responsible lawyer before the mark-up is sent.
=== END ADVICE ===
